# strum - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/strum/0.26.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/strum/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#strum)Strum

Strum is a set of macros and traits for working with enums and strings easier in Rust.

The full version of the README can be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/Peternator7/strum).

[§](https://docs.rs#including-strum-in-your-project)Including Strum in Your Project

Import strum and `strum_macros` into your project by adding the following lines to your
Cargo.toml. `strum_macros` contains the macros needed to derive all the traits in Strum.

```
[dependencies]
strum = "0.26"
strum_macros = "0.26"
# You can also access strum_macros exports directly through strum using the "derive" feature
strum = { version = "0.26", features = ["derive"] }
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [additional_](https://docs.rs/additional_attributes/index.html)- attributes
- Documentation for Additional Attributes

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- The `ParseError`enum is a collection of all the possible reasons an enum can fail to parse from a string.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AsStatic](https://docs.rs/trait.AsStaticRef.html)- Ref - Deprecated
- A cheap reference-to-reference conversion. Used to convert a value to a
reference value with `'static`lifetime within generic code.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/trait.EnumCount.html)- Count
- A trait for capturing the number of variants in Enum. This trait can be autoderived by
`strum_macros`.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/trait.EnumMessage.html)- Message
- Associates additional pieces of information with an Enum. This can be
autoimplemented by deriving `EnumMessage`and annotating your variants with`#[strum(message="...")]`.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/trait.EnumProperty.html)- Property
- `EnumProperty`is a trait that makes it possible to store additional information with enum variants. This trait is designed to be used with the macro of the same name in the- `strum_macros`crate. Currently, the only string literals are supported in attributes, the other methods will be implemented as additional attribute types become stabilized.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoEnumIterator.html)- Enum - Iterator
- This trait designates that an `Enum`can be iterated over. It can be auto generated using the`EnumIter`
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/trait.VariantArray.html)- Array
- A trait for retrieving a static array containing all the variants in an Enum.
This trait can be autoderived by `strum_macros`. For derived usage, all the variants in the enumerator need to be unit-types, which means you can’t autoderive enums with inner data in one or more variants. Consider using it alongside`EnumDiscriminants`
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/trait.VariantIterator.html)- Iterator
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/trait.VariantMetadata.html)- Metadata
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/trait.VariantNames.html)- Names
- A trait for retrieving the names of each variant in Enum. This trait can
be autoderived by `strum_macros`.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [AsRef](https://docs.rs/derive.AsRefStr.html)- Str - `derive`
- Converts enum variants to `&'a str`, where`'a`is the lifetime of the input enum reference.
- [Display](https://docs.rs/derive.Display.html)- `derive`
- Converts enum variants to strings.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumCount.html)- Count - `derive`
- Add a constant `usize`equal to the number of variants.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumDiscriminants.html)- Discriminants - `derive`
- Generate a new type with only the discriminant names.
- [EnumIs](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIs.html)
- Generated `is_*()`methods for each variant. E.g.`Color.is_red()`.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIter.html)- Iter - `derive`
- Creates a new type that iterates of the variants of an enum.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumMessage.html)- Message - `derive`
- Add a verbose message to an enum variant.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumProperty.html)- Property - `derive`
- Add custom properties to enum variants.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumString.html)- String - `derive`
- Converts strings to enum variants based on their name.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumTryAs.html)- TryAs
- Generated `try_as_*()`methods for all tuple-style variants. E.g.`Message.try_as_write()`.
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromRepr.html)- Repr - `derive`
- Add a function to enum that allows accessing variants by its discriminant
- [Into](https://docs.rs/derive.IntoStaticStr.html)- Static - Str - `derive`
- Implements `From<MyEnum> for &'static str`on an enum.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/derive.VariantArray.html)- Array - `derive`
- Adds a `'static`slice with all of the Enum’s variants.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/derive.VariantNames.html)- Names - `derive`
- Implements `Strum::VariantNames`which adds an associated constant`VARIANTS`which is a`'static`slice of discriminant names.

# sqlx - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sqlx/0.8.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sqlx/index.html

## Expand description

The async SQL toolkit for Rust, built with ❤️ by [the LaunchBadge team](https://www.launchbadge.com).

See our [README](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/README.md) to get started or [browse our example projects](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/examples).
Have a question? [Check our FAQ](https://www.github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/main/FAQ.md) or [open a discussion](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/discussions/new?category=q-a).

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-support)Runtime Support

SQLx supports both the [Tokio](https://www.tokio.rs) and [async-std](https://www.async.rs) runtimes.

You choose which runtime SQLx uses by default by enabling one of the following features:

- `runtime-async-std`
- `runtime-tokio`

The `runtime-actix` feature also exists but is an alias of `runtime-tokio`.

If more than one runtime feature is enabled, the Tokio runtime is used if a Tokio context exists on the current
thread, i.e. [ tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current()](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/runtime/struct.Handle.html#method.try_current) returns

`Ok`; `async-std` is used otherwise.Note that while SQLx no longer produces a compile error if zero or multiple runtime features are enabled,
which is useful for libraries building on top of it,
**the use of nearly any async function in the API will panic without at least one runtime feature enabled**.

The chief exception is the SQLite driver, which is runtime-agnostic, including its integration with the query macros.
However, `SqlitePool`*does* require runtime support for timeouts and spawning
internal management tasks.

[§](https://docs.rs#tls-support)TLS Support

For securely communicating with SQL servers over an untrusted network connection such as the internet, you can enable Transport Layer Security (TLS) by enabling one of the following features:

- `tls-native-tls`: Enables the- `native-tls`- SecureTransport on macOS.
- SChannel on Windows.
- OpenSSL on all other platforms.

- `tls-rustls`: Enables the- [rustls](https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/)backend, a cross-platform TLS library.- Only supports TLS revisions 1.2 and 1.3.
- If you get `HandshakeFailure`errors when using this feature, it likely means your database server does not support these newer revisions. This might be resolved by enabling or switching to the`tls-native-tls`feature.
- rustls supports several providers of cryptographic primitives. The default
(enabled when you use the `tls-rustls`feature or`tls-rustls-ring`) is the`ring`provider, which has fewer build-time dependencies but also has fewer features. Alternatively, you can use`tls-rustls-aws-lc-rs`to use the`aws-lc-rs`provider, which enables additional cipher suite support at the cost of more onerous build requirements (depending on platform support).

If more than one TLS feature is enabled, the `tls-native-tls` feature takes precedent so that it is only necessary to enable
it to see if it resolves the `HandshakeFailure` error without disabling `tls-rustls`.

Consult the user manual for your database to find the TLS versions it supports.

If your connection configuration requires a TLS upgrade but TLS support was not enabled, the connection attempt will return an error.

The legacy runtime+TLS combination feature flags are still supported, but for forward-compatibility, use of the separate runtime and TLS feature flags is recommended.

# sqlx_sqlite - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sqlx-sqlite/0.8.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sqlx_sqlite/index.html

## Expand description

**SQLite** database driver.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-linkage-is-semver-exempt)Note: linkage is semver-exempt.

This driver uses the `libsqlite3-sys` crate which links the native library for SQLite 3.
With the “sqlite” feature, we enable the `bundled` feature which builds and links SQLite from
source.

We reserve the right to upgrade the version of `libsqlite3-sys` as necessary to pick up new
`3.x.y` versions of SQLite.

Due to Cargo’s requirement that only one version of a crate that links a given native library
exists in the dependency graph at a time, using SQLx alongside another crate linking
`libsqlite3-sys` like `rusqlite` is a semver hazard.

If you are doing so, we recommend pinning the version of both SQLx and the other crate you’re
using to prevent a `cargo update` from breaking things, e.g.:

```
sqlx = { version = "=0.8.1", features = ["sqlite"] }
rusqlite = "=0.32.1"
```
and then upgrade these crates in lockstep when necessary.

[§](https://docs.rs#dynamic-linking)Dynamic linking

To dynamically link to a system SQLite library, the “sqlite-unbundled” feature can be used instead.

This allows updating SQLite independently of SQLx or using forked versions, but you must have
SQLite installed on the system or provide a path to the library at build time (See
[the  rusqlite README](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite?tab=readme-ov-file#notes-on-building-rusqlite-and-libsqlite3-sys)
for details).

It may result in link errors if the SQLite version is too old. Version `3.20.0` or newer is
recommended. It can increase build time due to the use of bindgen.

# rustledger_completion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-completion/0.19.1/rustledger_completion/

## Expand description

Editor-agnostic completion logic for Beancount sources.

This crate is the single source of truth for the completion logic
shared between the LSP (`rustledger-lsp`) and the WASM editor
(`rustledger-wasm`). It is deliberately pure: no clock access, no
`lsp-types`, no `wasm-bindgen`. Callers supply the live data
(account/currency/payee/tag/link string lists and “today’s” date)
and map the neutral [ CompletionCandidate](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html) results into their own
editor-specific item types.

The two responsibilities are:

- **Context detection**—- `offset_to_byte`- `PositionEncoding`- `classify_context`- `CompletionContext`
- **Candidate generation**— the- `*_candidates`functions produce neutral- `CompletionCandidate`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html)- Candidate
- A neutral, editor-agnostic completion candidate.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionContext.html)- Context
- Completion context detected from cursor position.
- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of a completion candidate.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.PositionEncoding.html)- Encoding
- How a position offset is encoded by the caller.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ACCOUNT_](https://docs.rs/constant.ACCOUNT_TYPES.html)- TYPES
- Standard Beancount account types.
- [DIRECTIVES](https://docs.rs/constant.DIRECTIVES.html)
- Standard Beancount directives.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_segment_candidates.html)- segment_ - candidates
- Candidates for the next account segment after a `prefix`.
- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates when starting an account name: the standard account types followed by every known account.
- [after_](https://docs.rs/fn.after_date_candidates.html)- date_ - candidates
- Candidates after a date: the directive keywords.
- [classify_](https://docs.rs/fn.classify_context.html)- context
- Classify the completion context from the text before the cursor.
- [currency_](https://docs.rs/fn.currency_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a currency after an amount.
- [line_](https://docs.rs/fn.line_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates at line start: a single date template using the supplied
`today`string (the crate is clock-free; each adapter passes its own date).
- [link_](https://docs.rs/fn.link_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a link after `^`(issue #1268). Mirrors`tag_candidates``label`and dropped in`insert_text`.
- [offset_](https://docs.rs/fn.offset_to_byte.html)- to_ - byte
- Map a position `offset`(in the given`encoding`) into a byte offset into`line`, clamped to a char boundary.
- [payee_](https://docs.rs/fn.payee_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a payee/narration inside a string. Returns all known
payees — the client filters (issue #1183, the `.take(20)`trap).
- [tag_](https://docs.rs/fn.tag_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a tag after `#`(issue #1268).

# rustledger_importer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-importer/0.19.1/rustledger_importer/

## Expand description

Import framework for rustledger

This crate provides the infrastructure for extracting transactions from bank statements, credit card statements, and other financial documents.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The import system is modeled after Python beancount’s bean-extract. It uses
a trait-based approach where each importer implements the [ Importer](https://docs.rs/trait.Importer.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_importer::{ImporterConfig, ImporterRegistry};
use std::path::Path;
// Build the per-call config (CSV in this example).
let config = ImporterConfig::csv()
    .account("Assets:Bank:Checking")
    .date_column("Date")
    .narration_column("Description")
    .amount_column("Amount")
    .build()
    .unwrap();
// Dispatch through the registry — picks OfxImporter for .ofx/.qfx,
// CsvImporter for .csv. Returns an error for unknown extensions.
let registry = ImporterRegistry::with_builtins();
// let result = registry.extract(Path::new("bank.csv"), &config)?;
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [ImporterConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ImporterConfig.html);
- `pub use ofx_importer::`- [OfxImporter](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/struct.OfxImporter.html);
- `pub use registry::`- [ImporterRegistry](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.ImporterRegistry.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Configuration for importers.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_importer/index.html)- importer
- CSV file importer.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_inference/index.html)- inference
- CSV format auto-inference.
- [ofx_](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/index.html)- importer
- OFX/QFX file importer.
- [registry](https://docs.rs/registry/index.html)
- Registry for importers.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

# rustledger_query - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-query/0.19.1/rustledger_query/

## Expand description

Beancount Query Language (BQL) engine.

This crate provides a SQL-like query language for analyzing Beancount ledger data.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

BQL is a specialized query language designed for financial data analysis. It operates on transaction postings while respecting double-entry bookkeeping constraints.

[§](https://docs.rs#query-types)Query Types

- `SELECT`- General purpose queries with filtering, grouping, and ordering
- `JOURNAL`- Shorthand for account statements
- `BALANCES`- Shorthand for account balance tables
- `PRINT`- Output filtered transactions in Beancount syntax

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_query::parse;
let query = parse("SELECT account, SUM(position) WHERE account ~ \"Expenses:\" GROUP BY account").unwrap();
println!("{:?}", query);
```

# rustledger_plugin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-plugin/0.19.1/rustledger_plugin/

## Expand description

Beancount WASM Plugin Runtime.

This crate provides a plugin system for extending Beancount’s functionality. Plugins can be written in any language that compiles to WebAssembly, or as native Rust code for maximum performance.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The plugin system uses wasmtime as the WASM runtime with `MessagePack`
serialization for passing data across the WASM boundary.

[§](https://docs.rs#plugin-types)Plugin Types

- **WASM Plugins**: Sandboxed plugins loaded from- `.wasm`files
- **Native Plugins**: Built-in plugins implemented in Rust

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-plugins-31)Built-in Plugins (31)

See the [plugin reference](https://rustledger.github.io/docs/reference/plugins) for the full list.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rustledger_plugin::{PluginManager, PluginInput, PluginOptions};
let mut manager = PluginManager::new();
manager.load(Path::new("my_plugin.wasm"))?;
let input = PluginInput {
    directives: vec![],
    options: PluginOptions::default(),
    config: None,
};
let output = manager.execute_all(input)?;
```

# postings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postings/0.2.0/postings/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#postings)postings

A small inverted-index core built around postings lists.

[§](https://docs.rs#scope-deliberate)Scope (deliberate)

- This crate is **index-only**: it does not store document content.
- It supports **candidate generation**with**no false negatives**(a caller may choose to verify candidates with an exact matcher).
- It uses a Lucene-style mental model: immutable “segments” (here: append-only batches) and logical deletes.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-modules)Optional modules

- `postings::codec`: low-level codecs (varint/gap) for postings payloads (in this repo).
- `postings::positional`(feature- `positional`): positional postings for phrase/proximity evaluation.
- `postings::raw`(feature- `raw-segment`): byte- and file-backed raw segment reader experiments.

[§](https://docs.rs#non-goals-for-now)Non-goals (for now)

- Full on-disk compaction
- Rich query language beyond candidate generation and sparse top-k scoring

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

Beancount validation rules.

This crate implements validation checks for beancount ledgers:

# pgcmp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pgcmp/0.1.0/pgcmp/

## Expand description

PostgreSQL schema comparison and migration testing, built for AI-assisted migration authoring.

`pgcmp` is primarily a CLI tool (`cargo install pgcmp`). It compares a
“new” database (the target schema you want) against an “old” database (the
current schema you have) and provides a verifiable feedback loop for
authoring a `MIGRATION.sql` that converges the old schema on the new one:

- `pgcmp pull`— snapshot both schemas to local SQL files.
- Write `MIGRATION.sql`(by hand or with an AI agent).
- `pgcmp test`— apply the migration in a transaction, diff the result against the target, report differences and row-count changes, roll back.
- Iterate until zero differences, then `pgcmp apply --commit`.

Migration files are validated with PostgreSQL’s own parser and must be
wrapped in a `BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... ROLLBACK;` envelope, so they are safe
to test repeatedly — nothing persists until `apply --commit` swaps the
final `ROLLBACK` for a `COMMIT`.

See the [README](https://github.com/appcove/pgcmp) for full documentation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [cli](https://docs.rs/cli/index.html)
- Clap argument definitions for the `pgcmp`CLI.
- [commands](https://docs.rs/commands/index.html)
- Implementations of the `init`,`pull`,`diff`,`test`, and`apply`commands.
- [comparison](https://docs.rs/comparison/index.html)
- Schema diffing logic.
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- `CONFIG.toml`parsing: connection settings for the new and old databases.
- [db](https://docs.rs/db/index.html)
- Database connectivity, schema extraction, and migration execution.
- [git](https://docs.rs/git/index.html)
- Git operations for schema snapshot directories.
- [memfs](https://docs.rs/memfs/index.html)
- In-memory filesystem helpers.
- [schema](https://docs.rs/schema/index.html)
- Schema object types and snapshot file writing.

# primeorder - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/primeorder/0.14.0/primeorder/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustcrypto-prime-order-elliptic-curve-formulas)[RustCrypto](https://github.com/rustcrypto/): Prime Order Elliptic Curve Formulas

Pure Rust implementation of complete addition formulas for prime order elliptic
curves ([Renes-Costello-Batina 2015](https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/1060) a.k.a. RCB).

Generic over field element implementations and curve equation coefficients.

[§](https://docs.rs#about)About

This crate provides a generic implementation of complete formulas for prime
order elliptic curves which are defined by the short [Weierstrass equation](https://crypto.stanford.edu/pbc/notes/elliptic/weier.html):

`y² = x³ + ax + b`It’s used to implement the following elliptic curves:

[§](https://docs.rs#-security-warning)⚠️ Security Warning

The elliptic curve arithmetic contained in this crate has never been independently audited!

This crate has been designed with the goal of ensuring that secret-dependent
operations are performed in constant time (using the `subtle` crate and
constant-time formulas). However, it has not been thoroughly assessed to ensure
that generated assembly is constant time on common CPU architectures.

# rustledger_ops - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-ops/0.19.1/rustledger_ops/

## Expand description

Pure operations on beancount directives.

This crate provides reusable functions for transforming and analyzing collections of beancount directives. All operations are pure — they take directives in and return results out, with no I/O or framework coupling.

Analogous to Python beancount’s `ops/` module.

[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

- `fingerprint`
- `dedup`
- `categorize`
- `merchants`
- `enrichment`
- `reconcile`
- `ml`- `std`, available on every target)
- `transfer`

# sim_lib_lang_cl - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-cl/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_cl/

## Expand description

Common Lisp surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Common Lisp surface syntax over
the shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ClGeneric](https://docs.rs/struct.ClGenericFunction.html)- Function
- CL-lite generic function (`defgeneric`/`defmethod`) over the dispatch organ.

- Condition-and-restart scope for CL-lite `handler-case`/`restart-case`.
- [ClLite](https://docs.rs/struct.ClLiteFormSpec.html)- Form - Spec
- Specification of one CL-lite surface form and the organ it routes to.

# SeaORM

#### SeaORM is a relational ORM to help you build web services in Rust with the familiarity of dynamic languages.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/stargazers/)

Please help us with maintaining SeaORM by completing the [SeaQL Community Survey 2025](https://www.sea-ql.org/community-survey/)!

[
Join our Discord server to chat with other members of the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Getting Started

Integration examples:

- [Actix v4 Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/actix_example)
- [Axum Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/axum_example)
- [GraphQL Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/graphql_example)
- [jsonrpsee Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/jsonrpsee_example)
- [Loco TODO Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/loco_example)/- [Loco REST Starter](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/loco_starter)
- [Poem Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/poem_example)
- [Rocket Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/rocket_example)/- [Rocket OpenAPI Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/rocket_okapi_example)
- [Salvo Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/salvo_example)
- [Tonic Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/tonic_example)
- [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example)

## Features

-
Async Relying on [SQLx](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx), SeaORM is a new library with async support from day 1.
-
Dynamic Built upon [SeaQuery](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query), SeaORM allows you to build complex dynamic queries.
-
Service Oriented Quickly build services that join, filter, sort and paginate data in REST, GraphQL and gRPC APIs.
-
Production Ready SeaORM is feature-rich, well-tested and used in production by companies and startups.

## A quick taste of SeaORM

### Entity

```
use *;
```
### Select

```
// find all models
let cakes:  = find.all.await?;
// find and filter
let chocolate:  = find
    .filter
    .all
    .await?;
// find one model
let cheese:  = find_by_id.one.await?;
let cheese: Model = cheese.unwrap;
// find related models (lazy)
let fruits:  = cheese.find_related.all.await?;
// find related models (eager)
let cake_with_fruits:  =
    find.find_with_related.all.await?;
```
### Nested Select

```
use DerivePartialModel;
let cakes:  = find
    .left_join
    .into_partial_model
    .all
    .await?;
```
### Insert

```
let apple = ActiveModel ;
let pear = ActiveModel ;
// insert one
let pear = pear.insert.await?;
// insert many
insert_many.exec.await?;
```
### Insert (advanced)

```
// insert many with returning (if supported by database)
let models:  = insert_many
    .exec_with_returning_many
    .await?;
models
    == Model ;
// insert with ON CONFLICT on primary key do nothing, with MySQL specific polyfill
let result = insert_many
    .on_conflict_do_nothing
    .exec
    .await?;
matches!;
```
### Update

```
use ;
let pear:  = find_by_id.one.await?;
let mut pear: ActiveModel = pear.unwrap.into;
pear.name = Set;
// update one
let pear: Model = pear.update.await?;
// update many: UPDATE "fruit" SET "cake_id" = NULL WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Apple%'
update_many
    .col_expr
    .filter
    .exec
    .await?;
```
### Save

```
let banana = ActiveModel ;
// create, because primary key `id` is `NotSet`
let mut banana = banana.save.await?;
banana.name = Set;
// update, because primary key `id` is `Set`
let banana = banana.save.await?;
```
### Delete

```
// delete one
let orange:  = find_by_id.one.await?;
let orange: Model = orange.unwrap;
delete
    .exec
    .await?;
// or simply
let orange:  = find_by_id.one.await?;
let orange: Model = orange.unwrap;
orange.delete.await?;
// delete many: DELETE FROM "fruit" WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Orange%'
delete_many
    .filter
    .exec
    .await?;
```
## 🧭 Seaography: instant GraphQL API

[Seaography](https://github.com/SeaQL/seaography) is a GraphQL framework built on top of SeaORM. Seaography allows you to build GraphQL resolvers quickly. With just a few commands, you can launch a GraphQL server from SeaORM entities!

Look at the [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example) to learn more.

## 🖥️ SeaORM Pro: Effortless Admin Panel

[SeaORM Pro](https://www.sea-ql.org/sea-orm-pro/) is an admin panel solution allowing you to quickly and easily launch an admin panel for your application - frontend development skills not required, but certainly nice to have!

Features:

- Full CRUD
- Built on React + GraphQL
- Built-in GraphQL resolver
- Customize the UI with simple TOML

Learn More

## Releases

[SeaORM 1.0](https://www.sea-ql.org/blog/2024-08-04-sea-orm-1.0/) is a stable release. The 1.x version will be updated until at least October 2025, and we'll decide whether to release a 2.0 version or extend the 1.x life cycle.

It doesn't mean that SeaORM is 'done', we've designed an architecture to allow us to deliver new features without major breaking changes. In fact, more features are coming!

[§](https://docs.rs#a-quick-taste-of-seaorm)A quick taste of SeaORM

[§](https://docs.rs#entity)Entity

```
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "cake")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub name: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {
    #[sea_orm(has_many = "super::fruit::Entity")]
    Fruit,
}
impl Related<super::fruit::Entity> for Entity {
    fn to() -> RelationDef {
        Relation::Fruit.def()
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#select)Select

```
// find all models
let cakes: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find().all(db).await?;
// find and filter
let chocolate: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find()
    .filter(cake::Column::Name.contains("chocolate"))
    .all(db)
    .await?;
// find one model
let cheese: Option<cake::Model> = Cake::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let cheese: cake::Model = cheese.unwrap();
// find related models (lazy)
let fruits: Vec<fruit::Model> = cheese.find_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
// find related models (eager)
let cake_with_fruits: Vec<(cake::Model, Vec<fruit::Model>)> =
    Cake::find().find_with_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nested-select)Nested Select

```
use sea_orm::DerivePartialModel;
#[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
#[sea_orm(entity = "cake::Entity", from_query_result)]
struct CakeWithFruit {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
    #[sea_orm(nested)]
    fruit: Option<Fruit>,
}
#[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
#[sea_orm(entity = "fruit::Entity", from_query_result)]
struct Fruit {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
}
let cakes: Vec<CakeWithFruit> = cake::Entity::find()
    .left_join(fruit::Entity)
    .into_partial_model()
    .all(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#insert)Insert

```
let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
    name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
};
let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
    name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default()
};
// insert one
let pear = pear.insert(db).await?;
// insert many
Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear]).exec(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#insert-advanced)Insert (advanced)

```
// insert many with returning (if supported by database)
let models: Vec<fruit::Model> = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
    .exec_with_returning_many(db)
    .await?;
models[0]
    == fruit::Model {
        id: 1,
        name: "Apple".to_owned(),
        cake_id: None,
    };
// insert with ON CONFLICT on primary key do nothing, with MySQL specific polyfill
let result = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
    .on_conflict_do_nothing()
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
matches!(result, TryInsertResult::Conflicted);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#update)Update

```
use sea_orm::sea_query::{Expr, Value};
let pear: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let mut pear: fruit::ActiveModel = pear.unwrap().into();
pear.name = Set("Sweet pear".to_owned());
// update one
let pear: fruit::Model = pear.update(db).await?;
// update many: UPDATE "fruit" SET "cake_id" = NULL WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Apple%'
Fruit::update_many()
    .col_expr(fruit::Column::CakeId, Expr::value(Value::Int(None)))
    .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Apple"))
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#save)Save

```
let banana = fruit::ActiveModel {
    id: NotSet,
    name: Set("Banana".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default()
};
// create, because primary key `id` is `NotSet`
let mut banana = banana.save(db).await?;
banana.name = Set("Banana Mongo".to_owned());
// update, because primary key `id` is `Set`
let banana = banana.save(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#delete)Delete

```
// delete one
let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
fruit::Entity::delete(orange.into_active_model())
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
// or simply
let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
orange.delete(db).await?;
// delete many: DELETE FROM "fruit" WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Orange%'
fruit::Entity::delete_many()
    .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Orange"))
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#-seaography-instant-graphql-api)🧭 Seaography: instant GraphQL API

[Seaography](https://github.com/SeaQL/seaography) is a GraphQL framework built on top of SeaORM. Seaography allows you to build GraphQL resolvers quickly. With just a few commands, you can launch a GraphQL server from SeaORM entities!

Look at the [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example) to learn more.

[SeaORM Pro](https://www.sea-ql.org/sea-orm-pro/) is an admin panel solution allowing you to quickly and easily launch an admin panel for your application - frontend development skills not required, but certainly nice to have!

Features:

- Full CRUD
- Built on React + GraphQL
- Built-in GraphQL resolver
- Customize the UI with simple TOML

Learn More

- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableArray.html)- Array
- An interface to get an array of values from the query result.
A type can only implement `ActiveEnum`or`TryGetableFromJson`, but not both. A blanket impl is provided for`TryGetableFromJson`, while the impl for`ActiveEnum`is provided by the`DeriveActiveEnum`macro. So as an end user you won’t normally touch this trait.
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableFromJson.html)- From - Json - `with-json`
- An interface to get a JSON from the query result
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableMany.html)- Many
- An interface to get a tuple value from the query result

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveEnum.html)- Active - Enum - `macros`
- A derive macro to implement `sea_orm::ActiveEnum`trait for enums.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveModel.html)- Active - Model - `macros`
- The DeriveActiveModel derive macro will implement ActiveModelTrait for ActiveModel which provides setters and getters for all active values in the active model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveModelBehavior.html)- Active - Model - Behavior - `macros`
- Models that a user can override
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveColumn.html)- Column - `macros`
- The DeriveColumn derive macro will implement [ColumnTrait] for Columns. It defines the identifier of each column by implementing Iden and IdenStatic. The EnumIter is also derived, allowing iteration over all enum variants.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveCustomColumn.html)- Custom - Column - `macros`
- Derive a column if column names are not in snake-case
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveDisplay.html)- Display - `macros`
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveEntity.html)- Entity - `macros`
- Create an Entity
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveEntityModel.html)- Entity - Model - `macros`
- This derive macro is the ‘almighty’ macro which automatically generates Entity, Column, and PrimaryKey from a given Model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveIden.html)- Iden - `macros`
- The DeriveIden derive macro will implement `sea_orm::sea_query::Iden`for simplify Iden implementation.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveIntoActiveModel.html)- Into - Active - Model - `macros`
- Derive into an active model
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveMigrationName.html)- Migration - Name - `macros`
- The DeriveMigrationName derive macro will implement `sea_orm_migration::MigrationName`for a migration.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveModel.html)- Model - `macros`
- The DeriveModel derive macro will implement ModelTrait for Model, which provides setters and getters for all attributes in the mod It also implements FromQueryResult to convert a query result into the corresponding Model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DerivePartialModel.html)- Partial - Model - `macros`
- The DerivePartialModel derive macro will implement [`sea_orm::PartialModelTrait`] for simplify partial model queries.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DerivePrimaryKey.html)- Primary - Key - `macros`
- The DerivePrimaryKey derive macro will implement [PrimaryKeyToColumn]
for PrimaryKey which defines tedious mappings between primary keys and columns.
The [EnumIter](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIter.html)is also derived, allowing iteration over all enum variants.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveRelatedEntity.html)- Related - Entity - `macros`
- The DeriveRelatedEntity derive macro will implement seaography::RelationBuilder for RelatedEntity enumeration.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveRelation.html)- Relation - `macros`
- The DeriveRelation derive macro will implement RelationTrait for Relation.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveValueType.html)- Value - Type - `macros`
- Implements traits for types that wrap a database value type.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIter.html)- Iter
- Creates a new type that iterates of the variants of an enum.
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromJsonQueryResult.html)- Json - Query - Result - `macros`
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromQueryResult.html)- Query - Result - `macros`
- Convert a query result into the corresponding Model.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
Async Relying on [SQLx](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx), SeaORM is a new library with async support from day 1.
-
Dynamic Built upon [SeaQuery](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query), SeaORM allows you to build complex dynamic queries.
-
Service Oriented Quickly build services that join, filter, sort and paginate data in REST, GraphQL and gRPC APIs.
-
Production Ready SeaORM is feature-rich, well-tested and used in production by companies and startups.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-quick-taste-of-seaorm)A quick taste of SeaORM

[§](https://docs.rs#entity)Entity

```
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "cake")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub name: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {
    #[sea_orm(has_many = "super::fruit::Entity")]
    Fruit,
}
impl Related<super::fruit::Entity> for Entity {
    fn to() -> RelationDef {
        Relation::Fruit.def()
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#select)Select

```
// find all models
let cakes: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find().all(db).await?;
// find and filter
let chocolate: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find()
    .filter(cake::Column::Name.contains("chocolate"))
    .all(db)
    .await?;
// find one model
let cheese: Option<cake::Model> = Cake::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let cheese: cake::Model = cheese.unwrap();
// find related models (lazy)
let fruits: Vec<fruit::Model> = cheese.find_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
// find related models (eager)
let cake_with_fruits: Vec<(cake::Model, Vec<fruit::Model>)> =
    Cake::find().find_with_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nested-select)Nested Select

```
use sea_orm::DerivePartialModel;
#[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
#[sea_orm(entity = "cake::Entity", from_query_result)]
struct CakeWithFruit {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
    #[sea_orm(nested)]
    fruit: Option<Fruit>,
}
#[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
#[sea_orm(entity = "fruit::Entity", from_query_result)]
struct Fruit {
    id: i32,
    name: String,
}
let cakes: Vec<CakeWithFruit> = cake::Entity::find()
    .left_join(fruit::Entity)
    .into_partial_model()
    .all(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#insert)Insert

```
let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
    name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
};
let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
    name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default()
};
// insert one
let pear = pear.insert(db).await?;
// insert many
Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear]).exec(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#insert-advanced)Insert (advanced)

```
// insert many with returning (if supported by database)
let models: Vec<fruit::Model> = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
    .exec_with_returning_many(db)
    .await?;
models[0]
    == fruit::Model {
        id: 1,
        name: "Apple".to_owned(),
        cake_id: None,
    };
// insert with ON CONFLICT on primary key do nothing, with MySQL specific polyfill
let result = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
    .on_conflict_do_nothing()
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
matches!(result, TryInsertResult::Conflicted);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#update)Update

```
use sea_orm::sea_query::{Expr, Value};
let pear: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let mut pear: fruit::ActiveModel = pear.unwrap().into();
pear.name = Set("Sweet pear".to_owned());
// update one
let pear: fruit::Model = pear.update(db).await?;
// update many: UPDATE "fruit" SET "cake_id" = NULL WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Apple%'
Fruit::update_many()
    .col_expr(fruit::Column::CakeId, Expr::value(Value::Int(None)))
    .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Apple"))
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#save)Save

```
let banana = fruit::ActiveModel {
    id: NotSet,
    name: Set("Banana".to_owned()),
    ..Default::default()
};
// create, because primary key `id` is `NotSet`
let mut banana = banana.save(db).await?;
banana.name = Set("Banana Mongo".to_owned());
// update, because primary key `id` is `Set`
let banana = banana.save(db).await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#delete)Delete

```
// delete one
let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
fruit::Entity::delete(orange.into_active_model())
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
// or simply
let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
orange.delete(db).await?;
// delete many: DELETE FROM "fruit" WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Orange%'
fruit::Entity::delete_many()
    .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Orange"))
    .exec(db)
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#-seaography-instant-graphql-api)🧭 Seaography: instant GraphQL API

[Seaography](https://github.com/SeaQL/seaography) is a GraphQL framework built on top of SeaORM. Seaography allows you to build GraphQL resolvers quickly. With just a few commands, you can launch a GraphQL server from SeaORM entities!

Look at the [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example) to learn more.

[§](https://docs.rs#-seaorm-pro-effortless-admin-panel)🖥️ SeaORM Pro: Effortless Admin Panel

[SeaORM Pro](https://www.sea-ql.org/sea-orm-pro/) is an admin panel solution allowing you to quickly and easily launch an admin panel for your application - frontend development skills not required, but certainly nice to have!

Features:

- Full CRUD
- Built on React + GraphQL
- Built-in GraphQL resolver
- Customize the UI with simple TOML

Learn More

[§](https://docs.rs#releases)Releases

[SeaORM 1.0](https://www.sea-ql.org/blog/2024-08-04-sea-orm-1.0/) is a stable release. The 1.x version will be updated until at least October 2025, and we’ll decide whether to release a 2.0 version or extend the 1.x life cycle.

It doesn’t mean that SeaORM is ‘done’, we’ve designed an architecture to allow us to deliver new features without major breaking changes. In fact, more features are coming!

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [ColIdx](https://docs.rs/trait.ColIdx.html)
- Column Index, used by `TryGetable``&str`and`usize`

- The generic API for a database connection that can perform query or execute statements. It abstracts database connection and transaction

- A trait for any type that can be turn into a cursor

- Identifier

- [Mock](https://docs.rs/trait.MockDatabaseTrait.html)- Database - Trait - `mock`
- A Trait for any type wanting to perform operations on the [MockDatabase](https://docs.rs/struct.MockDatabase.html)
- [Paginator](https://docs.rs/trait.PaginatorTrait.html)- Trait
- A Trait for any type that can paginate results
- [Proxy](https://docs.rs/trait.ProxyDatabaseTrait.html)- Database - Trait - `proxy`
- Defines the [ProxyDatabaseTrait](https://docs.rs/trait.ProxyDatabaseTrait.html)to save the functions

- A Trait for any type that can perform SELECT queries

- Any type that can build a [Statement](https://docs.rs/struct.Statement.html)
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/trait.StreamTrait.html)- Trait
- Stream query results
- [Transaction](https://docs.rs/trait.TransactionTrait.html)- Trait
- Spawn database transaction
- [TryFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.TryFromU64.html)- U64
- Try to convert a type to a u64
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetable.html)
- An interface to get a value from the query result
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableArray.html)- Array
- An interface to get an array of values from the query result.
A type can only implement `ActiveEnum`or`TryGetableFromJson`, but not both. A blanket impl is provided for`TryGetableFromJson`, while the impl for`ActiveEnum`is provided by the`DeriveActiveEnum`macro. So as an end user you won’t normally touch this trait.
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableFromJson.html)- From - Json - `with-json`
- An interface to get a JSON from the query result
- [TryGetable](https://docs.rs/trait.TryGetableMany.html)- Many
- An interface to get a tuple value from the query result

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveEnum.html)- Active - Enum - `macros`
- A derive macro to implement `sea_orm::ActiveEnum`trait for enums.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveModel.html)- Active - Model - `macros`
- The DeriveActiveModel derive macro will implement ActiveModelTrait for ActiveModel which provides setters and getters for all active values in the active model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveActiveModelBehavior.html)- Active - Model - Behavior - `macros`
- Models that a user can override
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveColumn.html)- Column - `macros`
- The DeriveColumn derive macro will implement [ColumnTrait] for Columns. It defines the identifier of each column by implementing Iden and IdenStatic. The EnumIter is also derived, allowing iteration over all enum variants.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveCustomColumn.html)- Custom - Column - `macros`
- Derive a column if column names are not in snake-case
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveDisplay.html)- Display - `macros`
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveEntity.html)- Entity - `macros`
- Create an Entity
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveEntityModel.html)- Entity - Model - `macros`
- This derive macro is the ‘almighty’ macro which automatically generates Entity, Column, and PrimaryKey from a given Model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveIden.html)- Iden - `macros`
- The DeriveIden derive macro will implement `sea_orm::sea_query::Iden`for simplify Iden implementation.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveIntoActiveModel.html)- Into - Active - Model - `macros`
- Derive into an active model
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveMigrationName.html)- Migration - Name - `macros`
- The DeriveMigrationName derive macro will implement `sea_orm_migration::MigrationName`for a migration.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveModel.html)- Model - `macros`
- The DeriveModel derive macro will implement ModelTrait for Model, which provides setters and getters for all attributes in the mod It also implements FromQueryResult to convert a query result into the corresponding Model.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DerivePartialModel.html)- Partial - Model - `macros`
- The DerivePartialModel derive macro will implement [`sea_orm::PartialModelTrait`] for simplify partial model queries.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DerivePrimaryKey.html)- Primary - Key - `macros`
- The DerivePrimaryKey derive macro will implement [PrimaryKeyToColumn]
for PrimaryKey which defines tedious mappings between primary keys and columns.
The [EnumIter](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIter.html)is also derived, allowing iteration over all enum variants.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveRelatedEntity.html)- Related - Entity - `macros`
- The DeriveRelatedEntity derive macro will implement seaography::RelationBuilder for RelatedEntity enumeration.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveRelation.html)- Relation - `macros`
- The DeriveRelation derive macro will implement RelationTrait for Relation.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/derive.DeriveValueType.html)- Value - Type - `macros`
- Implements traits for types that wrap a database value type.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/derive.EnumIter.html)- Iter
- Creates a new type that iterates of the variants of an enum.
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromJsonQueryResult.html)- Json - Query - Result - `macros`
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromQueryResult.html)- Query - Result - `macros`
- Convert a query result into the corresponding Model.

[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! + [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! ## Features
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//!
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! 1. Async
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!     Relying on [SQLx](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx), SeaORM is a new library with async support from day 1.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! 2. Dynamic
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!     Built upon [SeaQuery](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query), SeaORM allows you to build complex dynamic queries.
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! 3. Service Oriented
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!     Quickly build services that join, filter, sort and paginate data in REST, GraphQL and gRPC APIs.
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! 4. Production Ready
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!     SeaORM is feature-rich, well-tested and used in production by companies and startups.
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! ## A quick taste of SeaORM
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! ### Entity
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! ```
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! # #[cfg(feature = "macros")]
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! # mod entities {
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! # mod fruit {
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! # use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! # #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel)]
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! # #[sea_orm(table_name = "fruit")]
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! # pub struct Model {
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! #     #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! #     pub id: i32,
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! #     pub name: String,
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! #     pub cake_id: Option<i32>,
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! # }
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! # #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! # pub enum Relation {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! #     #[sea_orm(
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//! #         belongs_to = "super::cake::Entity",
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! #         from = "Column::CakeId",
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//! #         to = "super::cake::Column::Id"
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! #     )]
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//! #     Cake,
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! # }
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! # impl Related<super::cake::Entity> for Entity {
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//! #     fn to() -> RelationDef {
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! #         Relation::Cake.def()
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! #     }
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! # }
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! # impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! # }
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! # mod cake {
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//!
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel)]
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! #[sea_orm(table_name = "cake")]
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//! pub struct Model {
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!     #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//!     pub id: i32,
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!     pub name: String,
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//! }
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//! #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//! pub enum Relation {
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!     #[sea_orm(has_many = "super::fruit::Entity")]
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!     Fruit,
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//! }
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//! impl Related<super::fruit::Entity> for Entity {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!     fn to() -> RelationDef {
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!         Relation::Fruit.def()
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!     }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//! }
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//! # impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//! # }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! # }
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//! ```
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//!
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! ### Select
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//! ```
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! // find all models
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//! let cakes: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find().all(db).await?;
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//! // find and filter
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//! let chocolate: Vec<cake::Model> = Cake::find()
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!     .filter(cake::Column::Name.contains("chocolate"))
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!     .all(db)
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!     .await?;
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//! // find one model
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//! let cheese: Option<cake::Model> = Cake::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//! let cheese: cake::Model = cheese.unwrap();
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//! // find related models (lazy)
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//! let fruits: Vec<fruit::Model> = cheese.find_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//!
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! // find related models (eager)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! let cake_with_fruits: Vec<(cake::Model, Vec<fruit::Model>)> =
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//!     Cake::find().find_with_related(Fruit).all(db).await?;
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//!
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//! # Ok(())
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! # }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//! ```
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! ### Nested Select
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//!
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//! ```
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//! use sea_orm::DerivePartialModel;
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//! #[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//! #[sea_orm(entity = "cake::Entity", from_query_result)]
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//! struct CakeWithFruit {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!     id: i32,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!     name: String,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!     #[sea_orm(nested)]
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//!     fruit: Option<Fruit>,
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//! }
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//!
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//! #[derive(DerivePartialModel)]
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//! #[sea_orm(entity = "fruit::Entity", from_query_result)]
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! struct Fruit {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//!     id: i32,
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//!     name: String,
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//! }
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//!
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! let cakes: Vec<CakeWithFruit> = cake::Entity::find()
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!     .left_join(fruit::Entity)
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!     .into_partial_model()
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//!     .all(db)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//!     .await?;
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//! # Ok(())
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! # }
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//! ```
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! ### Insert
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! ```
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//! let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!     name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!     ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//! };
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//! let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//!     name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!     ..Default::default()
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//! };
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//! // insert one
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//! let pear = pear.insert(db).await?;
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//! # Ok(())
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//! # }
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//! # async fn function2(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//! # let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//! #     name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//! #     ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//! # };
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//! # let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//! #     name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//! #     ..Default::default()
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//! # };
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//!
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//! // insert many
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear]).exec(db).await?;
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//! # Ok(())
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! # }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//! ```
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//! ### Insert (advanced)
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! ```
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, TryInsertResult, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! # async fn function_1(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//! # let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//! #     name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//! #     ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//! # };
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//! # let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//! #     name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//! #     ..Default::default()
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//! # };
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//! // insert many with returning (if supported by database)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//! let models: Vec<fruit::Model> = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!     .exec_with_returning_many(db)
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//!     .await?;
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//! models[0]
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//!     == fruit::Model {
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//!         id: 1,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!         name: "Apple".to_owned(),
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!         cake_id: None,
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//!     };
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//! # Ok(())
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//! # }
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//!
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//! # async fn function_2(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//! # let apple = fruit::ActiveModel {
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//! #     name: Set("Apple".to_owned()),
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! #     ..Default::default() // no need to set primary key
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//! # };
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//! # let pear = fruit::ActiveModel {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//! #     name: Set("Pear".to_owned()),
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! #     ..Default::default()
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! # };
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//! // insert with ON CONFLICT on primary key do nothing, with MySQL specific polyfill
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//! let result = Fruit::insert_many([apple, pear])
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//!     .on_conflict_do_nothing()
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//!     .exec(db)
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//!     .await?;
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//!
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//! matches!(result, TryInsertResult::Conflicted);
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//! # Ok(())
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//! # }
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//! ```
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//! ### Update
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//! ```
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//! use sea_orm::sea_query::{Expr, Value};
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//!
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//! let pear: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//! let mut pear: fruit::ActiveModel = pear.unwrap().into();
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//!
[280](https://docs.rs#280)//! pear.name = Set("Sweet pear".to_owned());
[281](https://docs.rs#281)//!
[282](https://docs.rs#282)//! // update one
[283](https://docs.rs#283)//! let pear: fruit::Model = pear.update(db).await?;
[284](https://docs.rs#284)//!
[285](https://docs.rs#285)//! // update many: UPDATE "fruit" SET "cake_id" = NULL WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Apple%'
[286](https://docs.rs#286)//! Fruit::update_many()
[287](https://docs.rs#287)//!     .col_expr(fruit::Column::CakeId, Expr::value(Value::Int(None)))
[288](https://docs.rs#288)//!     .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Apple"))
[289](https://docs.rs#289)//!     .exec(db)
[290](https://docs.rs#290)//!     .await?;
[291](https://docs.rs#291)//!
[292](https://docs.rs#292)//! # Ok(())
[293](https://docs.rs#293)//! # }
[294](https://docs.rs#294)//! ```
[295](https://docs.rs#295)//! ### Save
[296](https://docs.rs#296)//! ```
[297](https://docs.rs#297)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[298](https://docs.rs#298)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[299](https://docs.rs#299)//! let banana = fruit::ActiveModel {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)//!     id: NotSet,
[301](https://docs.rs#301)//!     name: Set("Banana".to_owned()),
[302](https://docs.rs#302)//!     ..Default::default()
[303](https://docs.rs#303)//! };
[304](https://docs.rs#304)//!
[305](https://docs.rs#305)//! // create, because primary key `id` is `NotSet`
[306](https://docs.rs#306)//! let mut banana = banana.save(db).await?;
[307](https://docs.rs#307)//!
[308](https://docs.rs#308)//! banana.name = Set("Banana Mongo".to_owned());
[309](https://docs.rs#309)//!
[310](https://docs.rs#310)//! // update, because primary key `id` is `Set`
[311](https://docs.rs#311)//! let banana = banana.save(db).await?;
[312](https://docs.rs#312)//!
[313](https://docs.rs#313)//! # Ok(())
[314](https://docs.rs#314)//! # }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)//! ```
[316](https://docs.rs#316)//! ### Delete
[317](https://docs.rs#317)//! ```
[318](https://docs.rs#318)//! # use sea_orm::{DbConn, error::*, entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::*};
[319](https://docs.rs#319)//! # async fn function(db: &DbConn) -> Result<(), DbErr> {
[320](https://docs.rs#320)//! // delete one
[321](https://docs.rs#321)//! let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
[322](https://docs.rs#322)//! let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
[323](https://docs.rs#323)//! fruit::Entity::delete(orange.into_active_model())
[324](https://docs.rs#324)//!     .exec(db)
[325](https://docs.rs#325)//!     .await?;
[326](https://docs.rs#326)//!
[327](https://docs.rs#327)//! // or simply
[328](https://docs.rs#328)//! let orange: Option<fruit::Model> = Fruit::find_by_id(1).one(db).await?;
[329](https://docs.rs#329)//! let orange: fruit::Model = orange.unwrap();
[330](https://docs.rs#330)//! orange.delete(db).await?;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)//!
[332](https://docs.rs#332)//! // delete many: DELETE FROM "fruit" WHERE "fruit"."name" LIKE '%Orange%'
[333](https://docs.rs#333)//! fruit::Entity::delete_many()
[334](https://docs.rs#334)//!     .filter(fruit::Column::Name.contains("Orange"))
[335](https://docs.rs#335)//!     .exec(db)
[336](https://docs.rs#336)//!     .await?;
[337](https://docs.rs#337)//!
[338](https://docs.rs#338)//! # Ok(())
[339](https://docs.rs#339)//! # }
[340](https://docs.rs#340)//! ```

[342](https://docs.rs#342)//! ## 🧭 Seaography: instant GraphQL API
[343](https://docs.rs#343)//!
[344](https://docs.rs#344)//! [Seaography](https://github.com/SeaQL/seaography) is a GraphQL framework built on top of SeaORM. Seaography allows you to build GraphQL resolvers quickly. With just a few commands, you can launch a GraphQL server from SeaORM entities!
[345](https://docs.rs#345)//!
[346](https://docs.rs#346)//! Look at the [Seaography Example](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/tree/master/examples/seaography_example) to learn more.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)//!
[348](https://docs.rs#348)//! <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/master/examples/seaography_example/Seaography%20example.png"/>

}## Expand description

Value variants

We want the inner Value to be exactly 1 pointer sized, so anything larger should be boxed.

If the `hashable-value` feature is enabled, NaN == NaN, which contradicts Rust’s built-in
implementation of NaN != NaN.

use futures::TryStreamExt;
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake};
let mut cake_stream = cake::Entity::find()
    .order_by_asc(cake::Column::Id)
    .paginate(db, 50)

}

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sea_orm/executor/select.rs.html#915-923)

#### pub fn [into_model](https://docs.rs#method.into_model)<M>(self) -> [SelectorRaw](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectorRaw.html)<[SelectModel](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectModel.html)<M>>

```
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake, FromQueryResult};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, FromQueryResult)]
struct SelectResult {
    name: String,
    num_of_cakes: i32,
}
let res: Vec<SelectResult> = cake::Entity::find()
    .from_raw_sql(Statement::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."name", count("cake"."id") AS "num_of_cakes" FROM "cake""#,
        [],
    ))
    .into_model::<SelectResult>()
    .all(&db)
    .await?;
assert_eq!(
    res,
    [
        SelectResult {
            name: "Chocolate Forest".to_owned(),
            num_of_cakes: 1,
        },
        SelectResult {
            name: "New York Cheese".to_owned(),
            num_of_cakes: 1,
        },
    ]
);
assert_eq!(
    db.into_transaction_log(),
    [Transaction::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."name", count("cake"."id") AS "num_of_cakes" FROM "cake""#,
        []
    ),]
);
```

#### pub fn [into_json](https://docs.rs#method.into_json)(self) -> [SelectorRaw](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectorRaw.html)<[SelectModel](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectModel.html)<[JsonValue](https://docs.rs/query/enum.JsonValue.html)>>

**crate feature**only.

`with-json````
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake};
let res: Vec<serde_json::Value> = cake::Entity::find().from_raw_sql(
    Statement::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres, r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake""#, []
    )
)
.into_json()
.all(&db)
.await?;
assert_eq!(
    res,
    [
        serde_json::json!({
            "name": "Chocolate Forest",
            "num_of_cakes": 1,
        }),
        serde_json::json!({
            "name": "New York Cheese",
            "num_of_cakes": 1,
        }),
    ]
);
assert_eq!(
    db.into_transaction_log(),
    [
    Transaction::from_sql_and_values(
            DbBackend::Postgres, r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake""#, []
    ),
]);
```
Get an item from the Select query

```
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake};
let _: Option<cake::Model> = cake::Entity::find()
    .from_raw_sql(Statement::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake" WHERE "id" = $1"#,
        [1.into()],
    ))
    .one(&db)
    .await?;
assert_eq!(
    db.into_transaction_log(),
    [Transaction::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake" WHERE "id" = $1"#,
        [1.into()]
    ),]
);
```
Get all items from the Select query

```
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake};
let _: Vec<cake::Model> = cake::Entity::find()
    .from_raw_sql(Statement::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake""#,
        [],
    ))
    .all(&db)
    .await?;
assert_eq!(
    db.into_transaction_log(),
    [Transaction::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."id", "cake"."name" FROM "cake""#,
        []
    ),]
);
```

# IsolationLevel in sea_orm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-orm/1.1.20/sea_orm/enum.IsolationLevel.html

```
pub enum IsolationLevel {
    RepeatableRead,
    ReadCommitted,
    ReadUncommitted,
    Serializable,
}
```
## Expand description

Isolation level

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RepeatableRead)

### RepeatableRead

Consistent reads within the same transaction read the snapshot established by the first read.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ReadCommitted)

### ReadCommitted

Each consistent read, even within the same transaction, sets and reads its own fresh snapshot.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ReadUncommitted)

### ReadUncommitted

SELECT statements are performed in a nonlocking fashion, but a possible earlier version of a row might be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Serializable)

### Serializable

All statements of the current transaction can only see rows committed before the first query or data-modification statement was executed in this transaction.

An interface to get an array of values from the query result.
A type can only implement `ActiveEnum` or `TryGetableFromJson`, but not both.
A blanket impl is provided for `TryGetableFromJson`, while the impl for `ActiveEnum`
is provided by the `DeriveActiveEnum` macro. So as an end user you won’t normally
touch this trait.

#### fn [find_by_statement](https://docs.rs#method.find_by_statement)<C>(
    stmt: [Statement](https://docs.rs/struct.Statement.html),
) -> [SelectorRaw](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectorRaw.html)<[SelectGetableValue](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectGetableValue.html)<Self, C>>

```
use sea_orm::{entity::*, query::*, tests_cfg::cake, DeriveIden, EnumIter, TryGetableMany};
#[derive(EnumIter, DeriveIden)]
enum ResultCol {
    Name,
    NumOfCakes,
}
let res: Vec<(String, i32)> =
    <(String, i32)>::find_by_statement::<ResultCol>(Statement::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."name", count("cake"."id") AS "num_of_cakes" FROM "cake""#,
        [],
    ))
    .all(&db)
    .await?;
assert_eq!(
    res,
    [
        ("Chocolate Forest".to_owned(), 1),
        ("New York Cheese".to_owned(), 1),
    ]
);
assert_eq!(
    db.into_transaction_log(),
    [Transaction::from_sql_and_values(
        DbBackend::Postgres,
        r#"SELECT "cake"."name", count("cake"."id") AS "num_of_cakes" FROM "cake""#,
        []
    ),]
);
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# DeriveActiveEnum in sea_orm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-orm/1.1.20/sea_orm/derive.DeriveActiveEnum.html

```
#[derive(DeriveActiveEnum)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[sea_orm]
}
```
Available on

**crate feature**only.`macros`## Expand description

A derive macro to implement `sea_orm::ActiveEnum` trait for enums.

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

This derive macros can only be used on enums.

[§](https://docs.rs#macro-attributes)Macro Attributes

All macro attributes listed below have to be annotated in the form of `#[sea_orm(attr = value)]`.

-
For enum - `rs_type`: Define- `ActiveEnum::Value`- Possible values: `String`,`i8`,`i16`,`i32`,`i64`,`u8`,`u16`,`u32`,`u64`
- Note that value has to be passed as string, i.e. `rs_type = "i8"`

- Possible values:
- `db_type`: Define- `ColumnType`returned by- `ActiveEnum::db_type()`- Possible values: all available enum variants of `ColumnType`, e.g.`String(StringLen::None)`,`String(StringLen::N(1))`,`Integer`
- Note that value has to be passed as string, i.e. `db_type = "Integer"`

- Possible values: all available enum variants of
- `enum_name`: Define- `String`returned by- `ActiveEnum::name()`- This attribute is optional with default value being the name of enum in camel-case
- Note that value has to be passed as string, i.e. `enum_name = "MyEnum"`

-
For enum variant - `string_value`or- `num_value`:- For `string_value`, value should be passed as string, i.e.`string_value = "A"`- Due to the way internal Enums are automatically derived, the following restrictions apply:
- members cannot share identical `string_value`, case-insensitive.
- in principle, any future Titlecased Rust keywords are not valid `string_value`.

- members cannot share identical

- Due to the way internal Enums are automatically derived, the following restrictions apply:
- For `num_value`, value should be passed as integer, i.e.`num_value = 1`or`num_value = 1i32`
- Note that only one of it can be specified, and all variants of an enum have to annotate with the same `*_value`macro attribute

- For

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use sea_orm::{entity::prelude::*, DeriveActiveEnum};
#[derive(EnumIter, DeriveActiveEnum)]
#[sea_orm(rs_type = "i32", db_type = "Integer")]
pub enum Color {
    Black = 0,
    White = 1,
}
```

# DeriveEntityModel in sea_orm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-orm/1.1.20/sea_orm/derive.DeriveEntityModel.html

#[derive(DeriveEntityModel)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[sea_orm]
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`macros`## Expand description

This derive macro is the ‘almighty’ macro which automatically generates Entity, Column, and PrimaryKey from a given Model.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, Deserialize, Serialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "posts")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    #[sea_orm(column_type = "Text")]
    pub text: String,
}
```
Entity should always have a primary key.
Or, it will result in a compile error.
See [https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/issues/485](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/issues/485) for details.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "posts")]
pub struct Model {
    pub title: String,
    #[sea_orm(column_type = "Text")]
    pub text: String,
}
```

# EnumIter in sea_orm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-orm/1.1.20/sea_orm/derive.EnumIter.html

```
#[derive(EnumIter)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[strum]
}
```
## Expand description

Creates a new type that iterates of the variants of an enum.

Iterate over the variants of an Enum. Any additional data on your variants will be set to `Default::default()`.
The macro implements `strum::IntoEnumIterator` on your enum and creates a new type called `YourEnumIter` that is the iterator object.
You cannot derive `EnumIter` on any type with a lifetime bound (`<'a>`) because the iterator would surely
create [unbounded lifetimes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nomicon/unbounded-lifetimes.html).

# DeriveValueType in sea_orm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-orm/1.1.20/sea_orm/derive.DeriveValueType.html

```
#[derive(DeriveValueType)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[sea_orm]
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`macros`## Expand description

Implements traits for types that wrap a database value type.

This procedure macro implements `From<T> for Value`, `sea_orm::TryGetTable`, and
`sea_query::ValueType` for the wrapper type `T`.

The wrapped type must be `sea_orm::Value` compatible.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use sea_orm::DeriveValueType;
#[derive(DeriveValueType)]
struct MyString(String);
#[derive(DeriveValueType)]
struct MyNumber(i32);
```
It’s also possible to derive value type for enum-strings.
Basically the underlying type is String, and the custom must implement methods `to_str` and `from_str`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use sea_orm::{sea_query::ValueTypeErr, DeriveValueType};
#[derive(DeriveValueType)]
#[sea_orm(value_type = "String")]
pub enum Tag {
    Hard,
    Soft,
}
impl std::fmt::Display for Tag {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "{}",
            match self {
                Self::Hard => "hard",
                Self::Soft => "soft",
            }
        )
    }
}
impl std::str::FromStr for Tag {
    type Err = ValueTypeErr;
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        Ok(match s {
            "hard" => Self::Hard,
            "soft" => Self::Soft,
            _ => return Err(ValueTypeErr),
        })
    }
}
```
`from_str` defaults to `std::str::FromStr::from_str`. `to_str` defaults to `std::string::ToString::to_string`.
They can be overridden with custom functions.

```
use sea_orm::{sea_query::ValueTypeErr, DeriveValueType};
#[derive(DeriveValueType)]
#[sea_orm(
    value_type = "String",
    from_str = "Tag::from_str",
    to_str = "Tag::to_str"
)]
pub enum Tag {
    Color,
    Grey,
}
impl Tag {
    fn to_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Color => "color",
            Self::Grey => "grey",
        }
    }
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ValueTypeErr> {
        Ok(match s {
            "color" => Self::Color,
            "grey" => Self::Grey,
            _ => return Err(ValueTypeErr),
        })
    }
}
```
